text.p: Here are the highlights from Swiss newspapers on Thursday:
- The Langenthal porcelain factory, which is 90 percent-owned by Keramik Holding AG Laufen, will shut down production on February 1 and lay off some 90 employees.
- Swiss Federal Court ruled that EPA, a Swiss department store chain, may continue to sell Chanel perfume at a discount.
- Some 80 people will lose their jobs when wool spinning factory Interlaken AG shuts down operations next spring.
- Elesta AG Elektronik in Bad Ragaz will cut 157 of its 230 jobs by the end of February 1997.
- New York lawyers of Jewish Holocaust victims' relatives are calling for the boycotting of Swiss banks until Switzerland's judges allow close investigations of the bank accounts.
- Electronics group Zellweger Luwa is expecting a drop in profit to between 20 and 25 million Swiss francs for 1996, compared to 27.1 million in 1995.
- Swissair has decided not to sell its EDP subsidiary Atraxis after all, after a recent reassessment of the firm.

- Exactly 120 theatres in several countries, including several ones in the French-speaking region of Switzerland, will on December 1 at 7pm, perform the play "Le Fil", based upon the autobiographical novel of a 32-year-old Frenchman who is HIV positive. It is being performed in commemoration of World AIDS Day.
